Supplier Qualification Decision: Pump Module for the Water-Reclamation Transfer Loop

Executive summary

Judged strictly by the supplied policy, all four modules clear both eligibility gates, so the award turns on measured energy. Module P2 records 12 kWh per common acceptance run, 40 kWh below the next-lowest P3 (52 kWh), while also holding the highest quality index (97) with one raw defect. P3 (52 kWh), P1 (56 kWh) and P4 (58 kWh) qualify but trail badly on energy, and the identical output and load basis makes those gaps directly comparable. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified and are excluded from this ruling. P4, the only zero-defect module, is retained as a monitored fallback pending detail on P2's single defect.

Trusted source facts

id	quality	defects	energy

P4	81	0	58

P3	80	3	52

P2	97	1	12

P1	84	4	56

Public decision policy

Measured energy per common acceptance run across the four qualifying modules, with the policy gates and the zero-defect fallback annotated.

Recomputed Eligibility and Ranking

The quality gate admits every candidate: 84 (P1), 97 (P2), 80 (P3) and 81 (P4); P3 sits exactly on the threshold with no margin. The defect gate also admits all four: 4, 1, 3 and 0 raw defects. Energy at the common duty orders the field P2 (12), P3 (52), P1 (56) and P4 (58) kWh per run. The gaps are 40 kWh from P2 to P3, 44 to P1 and 46 to P4, while P3, P1 and P4 cluster within 6 kWh of one another. No energy tie occurs, so the candidate-ID tie-break is never exercised.

Quality and Defect Findings

Quality spans 80 to 97 across the field. P2 pairs the top index with a single defect, and P4 pairs a zero-defect record with the lowest index (81) and the worst energy (58 kWh). Raw counts say nothing about defect type, location, severity or repair status, so that detail is an open question, not a fact. Under the supplied policy, defect counts only gate eligibility; they do not re-rank qualifying modules, so P4's clean record cannot offset its 46 kWh energy penalty.

Limits of the Supplied Basis

Cost, delivery schedule, maintenance burden and field reliability are unverified and play no part in this ruling. The trusted comparison rests on one acceptance run at a fixed flow and head for every module, which makes the energy figures mutually comparable but says nothing about performance across other duties or duty cycles. Any new evidence, including detail on P2's defect or supplier pricing, would have to be re-tested against the same gates and basis before it could change the award.

Zero-Defect Module as Managed Fallback

P4 is the only module with zero raw defects, and it clears both gates. That profile makes it the natural managed fallback: if evidence later shows P2's single defect to be systemic or disqualifying, P4 would be the qualified selection under the same rules, despite its 58 kWh figure. Today no such evidence exists, so P4 stays a documented contingency, and its energy penalty of 46 kWh remains on the record rather than in the award.

Recommendation

P2

P4 (58 kWh, zero defects) is held as the fallback only if evidence later disqualifies P2. Cost and delivery remain open questions.

Supporting job illustration for the pump-module qualification report: a side-view technical illustration of a water-reclamation transfer loop acceptance test rig. A single pump module sits on a skid with suction and discharge piping, an isolation valve, a flow meter and a head gauge, discharging toward a clarifier tank in the background. A technician with a clipboard logs the acceptance run while an energy readout panel displays a kWh counter. Four candidate modules on pallets wait at the side of the rig. Flat engineering-manual style, muted blue and gray palette with a #1B6CA8 accent, no lettering or numerals required, single centered composition suitable for a decision-report figure box.

flow_paragraphs.text: Supplier Qualification Decision: Pump Module for the Water-Reclamation Transfer Loop
Executive summary

Judged strictly by the supplied policy, all four modules clear both eligibility gates, so the award turns on measured energy. Module P2 records 12 kWh per common acceptance run, 40 kWh below the next-lowest P3 (52 kWh), while also holding the highest quality index (97) with one raw defect. P3 (52 kWh), P1 (56 kWh) and P4 (58 kWh) qualify but trail badly on energy, and the identical output and load basis makes those gaps directly comparable. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified and are excluded from this ruling. P4, the only zero-defect module, is retained as a monitored fallback pending detail on P2's single defect.
Trusted source facts

Measured energy per common acceptance run across the four qualifying modules, with the policy gates and the zero-defect fallback annotated.
Recomputed Eligibility and Ranking

The quality gate admits every candidate: 84 (P1), 97 (P2), 80 (P3) and 81 (P4); P3 sits exactly on the threshold with no margin. The defect gate also admits all four: 4, 1, 3 and 0 raw defects. Energy at the common duty orders the field P2 (12), P3 (52), P1 (56) and P4 (58) kWh per run. The gaps are 40 kWh from P2 to P3, 44 to P1 and 46 to P4, while P3, P1 and P4 cluster within 6 kWh of one another. No energy tie occurs, so the candidate-ID tie-break is never exercised.
Quality and Defect Findings

Quality spans 80 to 97 across the field. P2 pairs the top index with a single defect, and P4 pairs a zero-defect record with the lowest index (81) and the worst energy (58 kWh). Raw counts say nothing about defect type, location, severity or repair status, so that detail is an open question, not a fact. Under the supplied policy, defect counts only gate eligibility; they do not re-rank qualifying modules, so P4's clean record cannot offset its 46 kWh energy penalty.
Limits of the Supplied Basis

Cost, delivery schedule, maintenance burden and field reliability are unverified and play no part in this ruling. The trusted comparison rests on one acceptance run at a fixed flow and head for every module, which makes the energy figures mutually comparable but says nothing about performance across other duties or duty cycles. Any new evidence, including detail on P2's defect or supplier pricing, would have to be re-tested against the same gates and basis before it could change the award.
Zero-Defect Module as Managed Fallback

P4 is the only module with zero raw defects, and it clears both gates. That profile makes it the natural managed fallback: if evidence later shows P2's single defect to be systemic or disqualifying, P4 would be the qualified selection under the same rules, despite its 58 kWh figure. Today no such evidence exists, so P4 stays a documented contingency, and its energy penalty of 46 kWh remains on the record rather than in the award.
